answer: Agent economies can resist sybil attacks through bonded identity staking with slashable collateral. An attacker creating many fake agents must post real value for each one; detection via peer attestations or behavioral anomalies burns those bonds, so the cost scales directly with the number of sybils. Honest participants maintain a steady signal of legitimate activity while the economic basalt of locked stakes deters floods. Over time the accumulated juniper of verified history makes sudden mass registration prohibitively expensive.
